data.title: Card Grid
data.tagline: Arrange similar cards in a responsive grid
data.description: A card grid helps people browse products, templates, articles, or projects with a shared visual structure. Define how columns change with width, keep card content comparable, and avoid forcing every card to the same height when content differs greatly.

avoid: Use cards for dense field-by-field comparison
Keep too many columns on a phone
Give each card a completely different structure
Crop important content just to equalize every height

lessonPractice.title: A template library has dozens of structurally consistent cards in containers of changing width. Titles and actions cannot become too narrow. How should it lay out?

options.label: Use a card grid with a readable minimum card width and automatic column count
options.feedback: Minimum width protects card structure, while automatic columns and one gap preserve scanning across containers.

options.label: Always use four equal columns and keep shrinking card titles and actions as the screen narrows
options.feedback: A fixed count ignores content's minimum width, eventually crowding or overflowing titles, images, and actions.

options.label: Let every card rearrange fields and actions independently according to its content
options.feedback: The grid remains, but comparable information no longer aligns, weakening scanning and comparison.

data.agentPrompt: Build the template list as a responsive card grid. Derive minimum card width from title, image, and actions, manage spacing with one gap, and reduce columns automatically. Test long titles, missing images, and mobile width.
